open.detail: UPDATE 2026-09-07 (offline repo read on main at 62638c17; no provider access). TWO of the four recorded claims hold, ONE holds with a corrected mechanism, and the central technical premise is REFUTED by the code on main. REFUTED: 'deletes an artifact family BEFORE calling OpenAI and re-inserting, one family at a time, never staged-then-swapped'. In all four writers in supabase/functions/indexing-v3-agent/index.ts - upsertMemoryCardsFromSections, upsertSectionIndexUnits, upsertVisualArtifacts, upsertCoreEmbeddingFields - the embeddingBatch await completes BEFORE sql.begin is entered, and the delete and re-insert share one Postgres transaction. A provider outage therefore aborts before any delete happens, and a failed insert rolls the delete back; the 'permanently empty family' failure mode does not follow from this code. tests/indexing-v3-agent.test.ts pins that ordering statically for all four. CONFIRMED: repair_strict_enrichment_gate_batch is invoked by nothing - every repo-wide hit is the migration, schema mirror, generated types, docs, or a schema-text assertion. CONFIRMED: no monitoring - needs_enrichment_artifacts appears in no script and no workflow. CONFIRMED WITH CORRECTED MECHANISM: both terminal states are excluded from claim eligibility forever, but by two different routes - claim_indexing_v3_agent_jobs excludes needs_enrichment_artifacts by NAME in 'status not in (...)', while failed is excluded through 'attempt_count < max_attempts', because agentFailureDecision only writes failed once attempts are spent. open.summary: Schema drift is gated against schema.sql only; the migration chain's semantics are never diffed against the mirror
open.detail: generate-drift-manifest.ts replays supabase/schema.sql and embeds ITS sha256; CI's db-reset-verify runs supabase migration up --local, proving the chain APPLIES but never diffing the result against schema.sql. A migration whose function or policy body diverges from the mirror passes every gate. Object-NAME parity does hold today (all create targets across 211 migrations resolve into schema.sql) but it is enforced by hand-written per-object tests, not systematically. FIX: after migration up --local, replay schema.sql into a second scratch database and diff schema_drift_snapshot() between the two. Fully offline and containerised, no provider access. open.summary: Ward Flow: sex and gender identity are one field, and that single field drives bed matching
open.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04: ward-model.ts declares 'sex: Sex' and no gender field anywhere. ward-eligibility.ts consumes it directly — unit.sexMix[movement.sex] and sexDesignationAccepts(unit.sexDesignation, movement.sex) — so a patient's bed eligibility is computed from that one value. open.summary: Phone-chrome reserve shift is FIXED on main (PR #2929); the residual is the ui-tools shard-3 settle assertion, not the product defect
open.detail: CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN 2026-09-20; NO LONGER PARKED. This is not a flaky test — it catches a real phone defect that also hits clinicians. The Differentials mode-nav row (49px) paints IN page flow, then ModeNavHeaderPortal moves it into the fixed phone header at ~315ms; content loses that height and every element rises 49px. usePhoneOverlayChromeReserve only republishes the measured 121px at ~423ms, so for ~110ms the whole page sits 49px too high. A press that straddles that correction lands on one control and releases on another: recorded trace shows pointerdown on the compare-open link at y 492-540, pointerup at the identical y hitting "Edit selection" because the link had moved to 443-491, and the browser retargeting the click to their common ancestor. The link never activates — no error, no navigation. scrollY is 0 throughout, so this is layout, not scrolling, and Playwright hit-target checks cannot see it because press and release were each individually on a real element. EVIDENCE: 0/41 reproductions through the repo runner (10x alone, 10x under 4 busy loops, 20x under 12, plus a full shard) — shard load is not the right kind of slowness. Under Chrome DevTools renderer throttling: 0/10 at 4x, 10/10 at 10x, 9/10 at 20x, and 0/10 at 10x when the phone chrome is allowed to settle first. That last row is the control. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW. (1) It is the PHONE click that fails, not the desktop one. tests/ui-tools.spec.ts:2928 is the test declaration; the test contains two compare-open clicks, and the URL CI recorded has no q=Pain, which matches the 390x844 phone block. Above the phone breakpoint the reserve publishes 0px and no addon row mounts, so desktop is not exposed. (2) The TO-UNBLOCK suggestion in this row does not work and is refuted: the destination "Loading presentation" role=status skeleton cannot be the settle signal, because it lives inside the destination route and only renders AFTER the URL commits. Proven by holding the destination response 20s — urlChangedAfterMs 20130, loadingSkeletonSeenAfterMs null. The "racing an unhydrated link" hypothesis is the right family but the wrong mechanism: the link is a plain next/link anchor from a Server Component, so a pre-hydration click would still navigate natively. The race is hydration-driven LAYOUT, not handlers. PRODUCT FIX LANDED as PR #2929, merged 2026-09-20 (commit 80cf3df6c69a); verified on origin/main, where publishPhoneOverlayChromeReserveNow appears in globals.css, phone-header-collapse-portal.tsx and use-phone-overlay-chrome-reserve.ts. open.detail: RESOLVED AS TO CAUSE 2026-09-16, by a live guest search of the production public corpus (read-only, user-authorised). CAUSE: page text came from page.get_text('text', sort=True), which orders text LINES by (y, x). A table whose cells wrap over several lines is therefore read straight ACROSS the columns. The served chunk from Clozapine Therapy - Initiation, Continuation and Ceasing Policy and Procedure (RKPG).pdf p16 reads 'Neutropenia Requires medical review. Stop clozapine. Contact WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L. Flu-like symptoms such 3.2% haematologist ...', binding the withhold threshold to the word 'Contact' rather than to 'Neutropenia'. Answer verification correctly refused to state a clozapine threshold from that text. Nothing was wrong with retrieval, ranking, chunk splitting or any guard. EVIDENCE: the live search returned 12 chunks across 7 WA clozapine guidelines (FSH, CAMHS, RKPG, NMHS x2, AKG, FSH GP Shared Care), so the documents are retrievable and admitted; exactly one of the 12 bound a blood-count threshold to a stop instruction, and that one was the scrambled chunk. CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN EARLIER REPORTING: an interim analysis in the same session stated 'zero of twelve chunks bind a figure to an action'. That was WRONG. The detector used only ANC and neutrophil, while these WA guidelines say WBC, neutropenia and agranulocytosis. The correct count is one of twelve. The wrong count briefly supported a corpus-gap reading; it is recorded here so the number is not re-quoted. FOURTH DISPROVED THEORY, added to the two already in this row: 'the expected document is scoped uploaded_local and is unretrievable by design' is FALSE - retrieval returned these documents to an unauthenticated caller. The alias tables also already absorb the corpus renames, so a stale expectedFiles entry is not the cause either. FIXED IN CODE: extract_pdf_assets.table_aware_page_text substitutes the cell-by-cell rendering find_tables() already computes for detected grid regions, leaving surrounding prose in reading order, with a retention guard that keeps the raw text if detection would swallow the page and an ignore rule for heuristic non-grid candidates. Reproduced on a synthetic three-column table with wrapped cells, mutation-tested (removing the fix reproduces the exact production string), covered by worker/python/test_extract_pdf_assets_table_reading_order.py (5 tests) with the full worker suite green at 27 passed. STILL OUTSTANDING AND OPERATOR-ONLY: the fix only applies to documents ingested after it ships, so every already-indexed chunk keeps the scrambled wording until re-ingested. Step 6 of scripts/operator-clozapine-retrieval-diagnosis.sql lists the affected chunks and collapses them into a per-document re-index worklist, using two fingerprints validated against the real production text. The eval cases stay red until that re-index runs. DO NOT relax the cases, the verification predicate or adjacentLabelledNumericBandConflicts - the refusal is correct behaviour on corrupted evidence.

open.summary: The Rockingham Peel clozapine guideline appears to state WBC below 1.5 for neutropenia, which is an ANC figure, and the evidence points at the source PDF rather than our extraction
open.detail: CLINICAL GOVERNANCE, NOT A SOFTWARE DEFECT, and it is the reason the extraction fix alone does not close this out. ANALYSIS 2026-09-16 from live public-corpus evidence. The served chunk of Clozapine Therapy - Initiation, Continuation and Ceasing Policy and Procedure (RKPG).pdf p16 states 'Neutropenia ... WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L' and 'Agranulocytosis ... WBC < 0.5 x 10 9/L'. Those are ANC figures. Australian practice: ANC below 1.5 x10^9/L is the red result requiring cessation, ANC below 0.5 defines agranulocytosis, and the WBC red threshold is 3.0 with green at WBC at or above 3.5 and ANC at or above 2.0. WHY THIS IS PROBABLY THE DOCUMENT AND NOT OUR PIPELINE, which is the whole point of this row: the line-major interleaving fixed in extract_pdf_assets splices whole LINES between columns, so it can move a line to the wrong place but it can never rewrite a word or split within a line. In the live text the run 'WBC < 1.5 x 10 9/L. Flu-like symptoms such' appears uninterrupted, bounded by 'Contact' before it and '3.2%' after it, both of which are fragments from other columns. That makes it a single source line from a single cell, so the label WBC and the value 1.5 were adjacent in the PDF itself. CORROBORATION from three other WA guidelines in the same corpus, extracted by the same pipeline: Clozapine Prescribing (NMHS) gives neutrophils at or above 2.0 and WBC at or above 3.5; Clozapine Prescribing, Administration and Monitoring (AKG) gives WBC at or above 3.5; Clozapine Therapy - Initiation and Continuation (FSH) gives neutrophils above 2.0, WBC above 3.5 and WBC below 3.0. Every one of them pairs WBC with 3.0 or 3.5 and neutrophils with 2.0. NONE pairs WBC with 1.5. RKPG is the outlier. CONFIDENCE: high, not certain. This is reasoning from extracted text of a document nobody on this side has opened. A clinician must read the source PDF before anything is escalated. NEXT STEPS: (1) read RKPG p16 in the original; (2) if it does say WBC below 1.5, raise it with Rockingham Peel Group as a clinical document error, because clinicians are reading that PDF directly and independently of this system; (3) only then decide what this knowledge base should do about the document, options being flag it, supersede it, or restrict it. DO NOT hand-edit corpus text to correct a source document. DO NOT relax the clozapine eval cases. The system refusing to answer clozapine threshold questions from this passage is the correct and protective behaviour, and it stays correct even after the re-index if the underlying document is genuinely wrong.

open.summary: Drift def_hash normaliser strips from any '--' to end of line, hiding 91 percent of the P03 seed function
open.detail: schema_drift_snapshot() computes a function def_hash as md5 of pg_get_functiondef with block comments, then '--[^\n]*', then all whitespace removed (supabase/migrations/20260706200000_schema_drift_snapshot.sql:89 and the 20260818090000 history-probe rewrite:97). The line-comment regex cannot tell a real comment from '--' inside a string literal. public.site_content_registry_baseline embeds the whole registry seed as a single-line dollar-quoted JSON blob, and the first '--' falls at offset 176107 inside a service URL (Next-Step---Drug-and-Alcohol-Services), so 91.1 percent of the definition - 1841007 normalised chars down to 164524 - is stripped before hashing. Measured, not inferred: replaying both the old and the new function body into a local Postgres 16 produced the identical pinned hash c2dc2183657bab3c994af7f18ddfcb9b even though the bodies differ, and that same replay reproduces the manifest value exactly for the unchanged body, so the control is sound. Consequence: check:drift and the post-merge live-drift workflow cannot see a change to that function's seed data after the first '--'. Every other function loses only genuine comments, which is the intended behaviour. A fix has to distinguish a comment from a literal - dollar-quoted bodies could be hashed unstripped, or the strip applied only outside string literals - and it changes def_hash for every function, so it needs a manifest regeneration in the same change.

open.summary: site_content_release_records_immutable is not 'enable always', so session_replication_role = replica bypasses the freeze's only structural protection
open.detail: READ FROM THE SCHEMA ON 2026-09-16, NOT EXPLOITED OR TESTED. supabase/schema.sql:12722-12724 creates site_content_release_records_immutable as an ordinary row trigger (before update or delete ... execute function guard_site_content_immutable_row). PostgreSQL does not fire an ordinary trigger when session_replication_role = 'replica', so a session that sets that GUC can UPDATE or DELETE rows of the frozen epoch-zero release with nothing raising. That is not a theoretical technique in this repository: scripts/check-site-content-control-plane.mjs:889-894 uses exactly it against a sibling table. TWO FURTHER GAPS IN THE SAME SEAL: the trigger covers only UPDATE and DELETE, so nothing prevents a row being INSERTED into a retained bootstrap release (it need only satisfy site_content_release_records_check1), and TRUNCATE is a statement-level event a row trigger never sees. Until the catalogue read-latency migration lands, the per-read bootstrap digest recomputation is the only thing that detects an inserted row, and it detects it after the fact — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS, stated honestly: setting session_replication_role needs the same superuser or postgres privilege an attacker would need to write the rows anyway, and such an attacker could equally replace the digest function. So the value here is against ACCIDENT — a half-applied migration, a bad replay, a partial restore, or a script that sets the GUC for an unrelated reason and then touches this table — not against a determined adversary. THE FIX: 'alter table public.site_content_release_records enable always trigger site_content_release_records_immutable', plus an 'enable always' before-insert trigger restricted to the retained bootstrap release ids and an 'enable always' before-truncate statement trigger. All transactional, no index build. SEQUENCE IT WITH the read-latency migration, which needs the same seal to justify removing the per-read digest; doing it separately means doing the same CREATE TRIGGER lock twice. GATE: SQL, so it ships as a new forward migration and needs an approved merge window. RUN check:site-content-control-plane in Docker FIRST — its own fixtures rely on session_replication_role on a sibling table, and an 'enable always' trigger on this one must be proven not to break them before merging.

open.summary: site_content_canonical_json is recursive plpgsql, so release activation will slow the same way the read path did once a release exceeds a couple of thousand records
open.detail: READ FROM THE SQL ON 2026-09-16, NOT MEASURED. site_content_canonical_json (supabase/schema.sql:12746) is a recursive plpgsql function: one invocation per JSON node, and a string_agg subquery over jsonb_each or jsonb_array_elements at every container. It defines EVERY fingerprint in the site-content control plane — release digest, contentHash, publicationVersion, governance and lineage hashes, plan and receipt identities — and is reimplemented in JS and pinned by tests/site-content-p03-baseline.test.ts, so it cannot be rewritten without invalidating stored digests across the live database. Measured proxy for its cost: the 843-record epoch-zero freeze canonicalises to 9,522,923 bytes across 164,820 JSON nodes (55,103 containers), i.e. ~165k plpgsql invocations and ~55k planned aggregate subqueries per pass, and two such passes per HTTP request cost about four seconds against live — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. The read path is being fixed by removing the calls. The WRITE path cannot be: site_content_dynamic_state_digest, site_content_release_digest, stage_site_content_sync_event, activate_site_content_release and rollback_site_content_release all canonicalise the full release by design and must keep doing so. Today that is tolerable because activation is rare and operator-driven. It scales linearly in node count, so a release of 2,000+ records makes activation slow in exactly the same way, and an activation that exceeds its statement timeout fails a publication rather than a page view. WHAT TO DO: nothing yet — this is a recorded scaling limit, not a defect. BEFORE the catalogue grows materially past the freeze, time one activation against a realistic release on a local Postgres (npm run check:site-content-control-plane already replays the control plane in Docker) and record the node-count-to-seconds curve, so the ceiling is known before an operator hits it mid-publication. DO NOT rewrite site_content_canonical_json to a set-based or C-backed equivalent as a performance fix: any byte-level difference changes every stored fingerprint, and a C extension cannot be installed by migration on Supabase.

open.summary: read_site_content_health() canonicalises the whole frozen corpus several times in one call
open.detail: COUNTED FROM THE SQL TEXT ON 2026-09-16, NOT MEASURED. Inside read_site_content_health() (supabase/schema.sql:15112-15342) there are four site_content_bootstrap_digest call sites — :15184 and :15185 in the bootstrap CTE (release_digest and dynamic_state_digest, which are equal for the bootstrap release) and :15285 and :15286 in the rollback CTE — plus two further whole-release aggregates via site_content_release_digest and a direct site_content_dynamic_state_digest. Each whole-corpus evaluation canonicalises 9,522,923 bytes and 164,820 JSON nodes through site_content_canonical_json, a recursive plpgsql function with one invocation per node, so each pass is roughly 165k plpgsql invocations and 55k planned aggregate subqueries. One investigation put the repeat count at five; four bootstrap_digest sites is what the current mirror contains, and how many are actually EVALUATED per call depends on planner materialisation and on which branches are reachable — nobody has measured it. THE FIX, and it is small: fold each PAIR that compares two stored columns to the same freshly computed digest into one evaluation (a scalar subquery or lateral computing the digest once and comparing both columns to it). No semantic change, roughly halves the work. RELATED: ledger #458SAC records the measured ~7s cost of this RPC against live and its 24 failed production deploys between 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-14, and asks for an EXPLAIN baseline; this row is the concrete mechanism and fix that #458SAC's next action was looking for, and the two should be read together. WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: the RPC is deliberately off the readiness path (src/lib/health-response.ts:148-158), so this is cost on the token-gated deep health probe and check:production-readiness, not on any user request. GATE: this is a SQL change, so it ships as a new forward migration and needs an approved merge window; run check:migration-role and check:function-grants, and regenerate the drift manifest. Context: docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md.

open.summary: Ward Flow's synthetic patient records are in 1629 published commits under a 2026-08-31 ruling the owner has deferred, not withdrawn
open.detail: REFRAMED 2026-09-20 after Codex correctly flagged the original wording on PR #2930, and RE-MEASURED the same day after a second Codex review found the exposure figures understated three times running. The original row was titled around the repository contradicting the 2026-09-01 assume-private ruling. THAT CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED and must not be re-raised: PR #2927 superseded that ruling in docs/ward-flow-owner-rulings-2026-09-01.md with the owner's 2026-09-20 decision, quoted verbatim - 'i will leave it public for now' - and recorded the first actual measurement (GitHub API: private=false, visibility=public). Leaving the row as written would have taught later sessions to treat a deliberate owner decision as an urgent unresolved defect, which is the same absence-read-as-signal failure this ledger exists to prevent. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is the 2026-08-31 ruling, section 5: 'Ward Flow is NOT to be pushed to a public repository as it stands.' The owner has DEFERRED that decision (2026-08-31 community audit, item 9: 'Defer for now - his decision, made knowing the eight invented patient records and three commits of history are public'), and deferred is not withdrawn. THE MEASURED BASIS IS FAR LARGER THAN THE RULING RECORDED. Files, pinned at commit 8d5cea0d1: the UMRNs are in 16 files where the ruling recorded 2, of which 14 CARRY the data and 2 only discuss it, and the names in 8 where it recorded 5. Commits: 1629 published commits carry the records, 1335 of them on origin/main - not the 3 the ruling recorded and every later restatement repeated. THE COMMIT FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it is what the ruling's own argument rests on: 'publishing a repository publishes its history'. Every earlier count used git log -S, the pickaxe, which finds commits where a string's PRESENCE CHANGES, not commits whose TREE CONTAINS it. There are only two distinct versions of src/components/ward-management/ward-patients-seed.ts in the entire repository and BOTH hold the eight records, so every commit carrying that file exposes them. Verified by enumerating the blob at that path across every commit reachable from the origin refs. WHY THE FILE FIGURE IS PINNED TO A SHA: every document that discusses this exposure - the two ruling files, this row, the inbox requests behind it - must name UM10000 or Talia Halloway to discuss it at all, and so joins the count. At the head of the commit that introduced the corrected paragraph the same commands already returned 20 and 12. Quote the pinned figure, never a fresh HEAD count, or each retelling makes the exposure look worse while nothing has changed. THREE SUCCESSIVE MEASUREMENTS RAN LOW, ALL IN THE SAME DIRECTION: 12 files / 4 commits, then 16 files / 3 commits, then this. The 12 came from searching UM100001, the first record of eight, missing four files carrying only one of the other seven. A privacy count is easy to take against one specimen, one branch, or one kind of change, and every such shortcut truncates - toward making publication look safer. Measure containment, not change, and pin the SHA. The records themselves are genuinely synthetic - the file header reasons the choice at length and the screens carry a visible synthetic-data marker - and the ruling's point was never that they are real, but that they do not look invented: eight full names, each with a UMRN and a date of birth, in a psychiatrist's public repository. The two options the owner approved at the time remain the options, and the containment count is the argument for the second: make the repository private, or replace every name and UMRN wherever they appear and publish a FRESH repository with a single initial commit, since rewriting 1629 commits of history is not a realistic alternative. NEXT ACTION IS THE OWNER'S, not an assistant's: this row exists to keep the deferral visible, not to reopen a settled decision.

open.summary: Draft PRs show a green PR-required gate while twelve heavy CI jobs stay skipped, so draft status is easy to misread as merge-ready
open.detail: Improve draft-status visibility (UI/docs/bot messaging) so a green draft is never treated as a full readiness signal. open.summary: The sign-off queue hides 52 of the 64 unsigned Formulation records, and a passing test pins the undercount
open.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-20 at HEAD, offline, no provider access. src/lib/developer-area/sign-off-queue.ts formulationFamily() reads ONLY (formulationContent as {mechanisms}).mechanisms and filters on mechanism.reviewStatus. The other 52 unsigned Formulation records - 46 contextual concepts and 6 guide modules, exactly the set ledger #DXJ70P describes - live in src/data/formulation-concepts.json, which formulationFamily() never opens. Verified: all 52 carry clinical_review_required, but under a 'review' key, not 'reviewStatus', so even if the file were read the existing filter would not match. Net effect: loadSignOffQueue() totals 1610 unsigned records across seven families (wa-mha-forms 54, formulation 12, differentials 232, dictionary 429, specifiers 603, therapy 205, sources 75) where the true figure is about 1662. WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A COUNTING NIT: the Developer Hub sign-off queue exists to be the one place that shows every clinical record awaiting a clinician's signature, and PR #2883 was titled 'Show every clinical record awaiting sign-off on the Developer Hub'. A clinician working that queue to zero would believe Formulation was done with 12 signatures. The 52 invisible records are the highest-consequence part of that family by #DXJ70P's own reasoning, because the guide modules INSTRUCT rather than define - guide-08 makes a specific claim about NICE NG225 advising against risk stratification for predicting suicide or repeat self-harm, and no clause in any of them has been checked against a primary source. THE GUARD IS INVERTED: tests/sign-off-queue.test.ts:25 asserts formulation: 12, so the test suite currently enforces the undercount and would go red on the fix. Fixing the count without changing that line is not possible, and the line must be changed deliberately rather than by a tool. NEXT ACTION: extend formulationFamily() to read formulation-concepts.json concepts and guides, match on the 'review' field these records actually carry, give each row an href to its page, and update the pinned expectation to 64 in the same change. Not a RAG surface; no retrieval or ranking code is touched. Offline gate: npm run test:focused -- --files tests/sign-off-queue.test.ts.

open.summary: A Playwright run whose own web server fails to start silently reuses another server and reports green
open.detail: Observed 2026-09-20 while writing tests/ui-patient-number-field.spec.ts. The agent running scripts/run-playwright.mjs had its own webServer fail to start because a concurrent session already held the port; the runner did not stop. It proceeded against THAT other server and reported a green pass. The run was re-done cleanly afterwards and the reported result is sound, but the hazard is not the individual run — it is that a browser gate can report success without ever exercising the tree it claims to test. This is the same class of failure as a gate piped into tail (exit code masked) and as CLINICAL_HAZARD_CONTROLS_PASS printing while a named proof file had been emptied: a signal that cannot fail is worse than no signal, because it is trusted. It matters more here than in most repos because verification evidence is quoted verbatim into PR bodies and the ledger, so a contaminated run propagates as fact. NEXT: make Playwright webServer startup failure fatal rather than falling back to an already-listening port — either set reuseExistingServer:false for CI/agent runs, or have run-playwright.mjs confirm the server it connects to is the one it started (the repo already has /api/local-project-id for exactly this identity question, used by npm run ensure). Add a contract test that a failed server start exits non-zero. Note npm run ensure already solves the adjacent problem correctly and is the pattern to copy.

open.summary: Two Firefox failures survive the 2026-09-20 triage: the document-viewer hit counter and the tools Forms panel, both a click whose state change never lands
open.detail: Read the Playwright trace from the failing run BEFORE proposing any fix; playwright.config.ts sets trace: retain-on-failure so it exists, and its After-DOM snapshot of the click answers this in minutes. THE TWO: (1) ui-smoke.spec.ts "search regressions avoid fetch errors and open viewer hits @critical" - after clicking Next document search hit, "Hit 2 of 2" never appears (element NOT FOUND, not hidden); (2) ui-tools.spec.ts "tool links point to the expected in-app modes" - the Forms complementary panel resolves to zero elements, on the 4th of 6 loop passes, while Services with an identical /?mode=<id> href passes. SAME SHAPE, so probably one shared Firefox cause. RULED OUT by two independent agent reads, do not re-derive: text split across elements (Playwright elementText flattens descendants and JSX/SSR comment separators); a collapsed <details> or any CSS cause (a hidden node still matches, and would report hidden not not-found - no stylesheet removes a node from the DOM); scrollIntoView/smooth scroll (suite-wide reducedMotion: reduce makes resolveScrollBehavior return auto); keyboard/focus; a click intercepted by the fixed composer (Playwright's hit-target interceptor blocks and retries, failing AT the click); Forms-specific data or markup (tools-catalog.ts Forms and Services are the same shape, and DetailActions renders the href link unconditionally). LEADING CANDIDATES: for (1), the handler firing zero times or twice - with exactly 2 hits, (i+d+2)%2 returns to 0 either way - with the exclusive-accordion open-attribute fight at source-panels.tsx:1063 as a plausible Gecko-specific trigger; for (2), the panel's hardcoded aria-labelledby id resolving against a hidden duplicate page root (the #093 failure mode visibleByTestId exists for), or the bare focus() at tools-search-results-page.tsx:470 scrolling late. NEITHER IS PROVEN. Why: Why it matters - if the click genuinely no-ops, a Firefox user cannot page through document search hits at all, which is a clinical reading path; if it double-fires it is a harness artefact and the test should assert the active chunk id rather than a modulo-2 counter. Context: Six Firefox failures in main run 35503893104; four fixed in PRs #2932 and #2933, these two left. Parent row #9Z197J. Owner: unknown - depends on what the trace shows. Confidence: high that the cause is shared and not CSS/text-matching; low on any single mechanism. Depends on: the egress row - the trace could not be downloaded from the cloud container.

open.summary: Three blocked hostnames stop any cloud session running Firefox/WebKit or reading a CI trace, so browser failures can only be reasoned about from logs
open.detail: Add cdn.playwright.dev, playwright.download.prss.microsoft.com and *.blob.core.windows.net to the Claude Cloud environment's egress allowlist; owner action in the environment settings, no repo change. THE THREE, each verified by a real request, not inferred: the first two are the ONLY mirrors in playwright-core 1.63.0's PLAYWRIGHT_CDN_MIRRORS (the old *.azureedge.net entries were removed in this version, so allowlisting those achieves nothing) and both return 403 request blocked; the third serves GitHub Actions artifacts, and an artifact download redirects there and returns CONNECT tunnel failed 403, which is why a retained Playwright trace cannot be fetched. ALSO CHECKED AND DEAD: ftp/archive/download.mozilla.org, snapcraft, flathub, the mozillateam PPA, codeload, and the npm @playwright/browser-firefox package (a 15KB stub that downloads from the same blocked CDN). A stock apt/tarball Firefox is NOT a substitute at any version - Playwright launches with -juggler-pipe and waits for "Juggler listening to the pipe", which only its own patched build emits - and there is no channel: firefox and no PLAYWRIGHT_FIREFOX_EXECUTABLE_PATH; the repo's PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH is its own invention and Chromium-only. Why: This is the constraint that shaped the whole 2026-09-20 triage. Four Firefox failures were fixed without a single Firefox run, and the dark-mode one was nearly written up as a broken app for every Firefox and Safari user before a cross-check refuted it; the two that remain are stuck precisely because the trace that would settle them is behind the third hostname. Context: Also worth knowing separately - the preinstalled Chromium is 141 (revision 1194) where playwright-core 1.63.0 pins revision 1243 / Chrome 153, so even local Chromium proof is twelve majors behind CI. Owner: Josh - environment settings. Confidence: high; every claim above was checked by running the request or reading node_modules/playwright-core. Depends on: nothing.
